title: Nurse hours against complaints, findings and State action at the 79 homes
question: Do the homes that report fewer nurse hours draw more complaints, substantiated findings or State action for their size?
finding: 77 homes with both figures. Lowest quarter on nurse hours: 0.891 allegations and 0.0836 substantiated complaints and incidents per 1,000 resident days, 2.13 State actions per 100 beds; highest quarter: 0.812, 0.0558 and 2.41. Rank correlation of nurse hours with the allegation rate -0.10, with the substantiated rate -0.25.
how: Homes ranked by the federal file's reported total nurse staffing hours per resident per day (October 2026) and cut into four equal bands; rates pooled as in chf-groups-compared. Spearman rank correlation across homes.
limits: Nurse hours are a recent quarter set against three years of complaints. Homes with more complex residents staff more and also see more incidents; short-stay homes report more. A correlation across 79 chosen homes is not a cause.
